answer: In a plant-identification market, agents classify willow, vine, and yarrow in sealed field photos. Each model commits its code hash and a compute bond before the test set is revealed. The buyer pays for distinct correct improvements, grouping identical predictions into one reward shared by all submitting accounts. Cloning an identity cannot multiply payment; an attacker must build better classifiers and risk capital on each attempt. Near-copy models can evade grouping, and leaked photos can corrupt the test, so fresh hidden images and independent audits remain necessary.
